data.title: Spotify Artist Alerts: Follow Artists, Get Notified on Events

epic.spec:
# Spotify Artist Alerts: Follow Artists, Get Notified on Events

## Overview

Enable users to follow music artists and receive multi-channel notifications (in-app, email, SMS) when followed artists have events in Austria. Artists can be sourced from Spotify (auto-import top artists) or added manually (search + free-text). The system continuously monitors the ~109K+ event database for matches against followed artists and fans out notifications to all followers.

**Existing foundation**: Spotify OAuth, token management, basic `.includes()` matching, `spotify_artist_matches` table, `notifications` table with `spotify_match` type, NotificationBell with Realtime subscriptions -- all exist but are incomplete or disconnected.

## Scope

### In scope
- `followed_artists` table decoupled from Spotify (supports both Spotify and manual sources)
- Refactor Spotify OAuth callback to populate `followed_artists` instead of `spotify_artist_matches`
- Artist management UI: top 10 pre-selected from Spotify, search (Spotify API), manual add, follow/unfollow
- Spotify search API integration (Client Credentials flow for app-level access)
- Improved artist-event matching engine using `pg_trgm` word_similarity + guards for short names
- Post-scrape matching pipeline via Supabase Edge Function + pg_cron
- Notification fan-out: in-app (existing infra), email (Resend), SMS (Twilio)
- User notification preferences (channel selection, phone number)
- Notification deduplication (no duplicate alerts for same artist+event)
- GDPR/DSGVO compliant opt-in for email/SMS

### Out of scope
- Spotify Extended Quota Mode application (documented as known limitation)
- Push notifications (web push / mobile)
- Geographic filtering on alerts (e.g. "only Wien")
- AI/ML artist-event matching (semantic embeddings)
- Admin dashboard for pipeline health monitoring
- Digest mode (daily/weekly email summary) -- future enhancement

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph User Actions
        A[Connect Spotify] --> B[OAuth Callback]
        B --> C[Fetch Top 50 Artists]
        C --> D[Pre-select Top 10]
        D --> E[Artist Management UI]
        F[Manual Search] --> E
        G[Free-text Add] --> E
        E --> H[followed_artists table]
    end

    subgraph Matching Pipeline
        I[Scraper runs] --> J[Events upserted to DB]
        J --> K[pg_cron triggers Edge Function]
        K --> L[pg_trgm word_similarity matching]
        L --> M{Match found?}
        M -->|Yes| N[Check dedup: already notified?]
        N -->|No| O[Insert artist_event_notifications]
        N -->|Yes| P[Skip]
    end

    subgraph Notification Fan-out
        O --> Q[Insert into notifications table]
        Q --> R[Supabase Realtime - In-App]
        Q --> S[Resend - Email]
        Q --> T[Twilio - SMS]
    end

    H --> L
```

```mermaid
erDiagram
    profiles ||--o{ followed_artists : has
    profiles ||--o| notification_preferences : has
    followed_artists }o--o{ artist_event_notifications : generates
    events }o--o{ artist_event_notifications : matched
    artist_event_notifications ||--o{ notifications : creates

    followed_artists {
        uuid id PK
        uuid user_id FK
        text artist_name
        text artist_name_normalized
        text spotify_artist_id "nullable"
        text spotify_image_url "nullable"
        text source "spotify or manual"
        boolean active "default true"
        timestamptz created_at
    }

    artist_event_notifications {
        uuid id PK
        uuid user_id FK
        uuid event_id FK
        text artist_name
        real match_score
        text match_source "title or description"
        boolean notified "default false"
        timestamptz notified_at
        timestamptz created_at
        constraint uq "UNIQUE user_id event_id artist_name"
    }

    notification_preferences {
        uuid id PK
        uuid user_id FK "UNIQUE"
        boolean artist_alerts_enabled "default true"
        boolean channel_in_app "default true"
        boolean channel_email "default false"
        boolean channel_sms "default false"
        text phone_number "nullable E.164"
        text email_override "nullable"
        timestamptz created_at
        timestamptz updated_at
    }
```

## Phases

### Phase 1: Data Foundation (Tasks 1-2)
Database schema, migrations, RLS policies, pg_trgm setup, followed_artists table, Spotify callback refactor.

### Phase 2: Artist Discovery (Tasks 3-4)
Spotify search API (Client Credentials), artist management UI with top 10 pre-selection, manual add, search.

### Phase 3: Matching Engine (Task 5)
pg_trgm-based matching with word_similarity, minimum name length guards, normalization, deduplication.

### Phase 4: Pipeline and Notifications (Tasks 6-8)
Edge Function for post-scrape matching, pg_cron scheduling, Resend email integration, Twilio SMS integration.

### Phase 5: Preferences and Polish (Tasks 9-10)
Notification preferences UI, phone number validation, E2E testing, documentation updates.

## Alternatives Considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Decision |
|--------|------|------|----------|
| Client-side matching (current) | Simple | Does not scale, no re-matching | **Rejected** -- move to server-side pg_trgm |
| Database trigger on event INSERT | Real-time, no cron needed | Write amplification on bulk scraper upserts, Edge Function concurrency limits | **Rejected** -- too many triggers during scraper runs |
| pg_cron + Edge Function (chosen) | Batched, efficient, controllable frequency | Slight delay (minutes, not real-time) | **Chosen** -- best balance of efficiency and reliability |
| Embedding-based semantic matching | Handles misspellings, translations | Overkill, complex infrastructure, expensive | **Deferred** -- pg_trgm sufficient for artist names |
| Supabase Auth Spotify provider | Built-in, less code | Cannot control token storage, no Client Credentials flow | **Rejected** -- keep custom OAuth for token control |

## Non-Functional Requirements

- **Matching latency**: < 5 minutes from event insertion to notification delivery
- **False positive rate**: < 5% for artist names >= 4 characters
- **Notification delivery**: In-app immediate (Realtime), email within 1 minute, SMS within 2 minutes
- **Database performance**: pg_trgm GIN index on events.title, matching query < 500ms for 200 followed artists against 109K events
- **Token security**: Spotify refresh tokens not accessible client-side (RLS deny on SELECT or Vault)
- **GDPR compliance**: Email/SMS off by default, explicit opt-in required, unsubscribe in every email

## Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| Spotify Dev Mode 5-user limit | Certain | High -- blocks public launch | Ship manual-first. Spotify behind feature flag. Apply for Extended Quota separately. |
| False positive matches for short names | High | Medium -- spam, user trust | Minimum 3-char names use exact word match; 4+ use pg_trgm threshold 0.6; 1-2 char names blocked |
| pg_cron not available on free tier | Medium | High -- no automated pipeline | Check plan tier. Fallback: manual npm script triggered post-scrape |
| Resend/Twilio API failures | Low | Medium -- missed notifications | Retry queue with 3 attempts, exponential backoff |
| spotify_refresh_token exposed client-side | Already present | High -- security breach | Add RLS policy: DENY SELECT on spotify_refresh_token for authenticated users |
| Notification flood from festival events | Medium | Medium -- user annoyance | Deduplicate: max 1 notification per (user, event) regardless of how many artists match |

## Rollout Plan

1. **Phase 1-2**: Deploy DB schema + artist management UI. Manual-only follows first.
2. **Phase 3**: Deploy matching engine. Dry-run mode first, log matches without notifying.
3. **Phase 4**: Enable in-app notifications. Monitor for false positives. Then enable email, then SMS.
4. **Phase 5**: Preferences UI. Full rollout.

**Rollback**: Each phase independently revertible. Edge Function can be disabled via Supabase dashboard.

## Metrics

- Followed artists count per user (avg, p50, p90)
- Match accuracy (false positive reports / total matches)
- Notification delivery rate per channel
- Spotify connect rate (connects / profile views)
- Artist alert click-through rate

## Quick commands

```bash
# Run matching pipeline manually (after implementation)
npx tsx src/scripts/match-artists.ts --dry-run

# Check followed artists for a user
npx tsx src/scripts/match-artists.ts --user-id <uuid> --dry-run

# Run tests
npm test
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] Users can follow artists via Spotify (top artists auto-imported) or manually (search + free-text)
- [ ] Artist management UI shows top 10 pre-selected from Spotify with toggle on/off
- [ ] Spotify search returns artist results for connected and non-connected users
- [ ] When a new event with a followed artist appears, all followers are notified
- [ ] Notifications delivered via in-app (immediate), email (Resend), and SMS (Twilio)
- [ ] No duplicate notifications for the same user+event+artist combination
- [ ] User can configure notification channels (in-app/email/SMS) and provide phone number
- [ ] Email/SMS are off by default (GDPR opt-in)
- [ ] Short artist names (< 4 chars) use stricter matching to avoid false positives
- [ ] Spotify refresh tokens are not accessible client-side
- [ ] pg_trgm GIN index ensures matching performance at scale
- [ ] All existing tests pass, new features have test coverage
- [ ] CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, HANDOFF.md updated

## References

- Existing Spotify code: `src/lib/spotify.ts`, `src/app/auth/spotify/callback/route.ts`, `src/app/spotify-matches/page.tsx`
- Notification infra: `src/components/Notifications/NotificationBell.tsx`, `src/app/notifications/page.tsx`
- Fuzzy matching: `src/lib/dedup/jaro-winkler.ts`
- DB sync pipeline: `src/lib/db/supabase-sync.ts`
- Scraper entry: `src/scripts/scrape.ts`
- Auth context: `src/lib/supabase/auth-context.tsx`
- [Spotify Web API - Top Artists](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/reference/get-users-top-artists-and-tracks)
- [Spotify Web API - Search](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/reference/search)
- [Spotify Client Credentials Flow](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/tutorials/client-credentials-flow)
- [PostgreSQL pg_trgm](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgtrgm.html)
- [Supabase Edge Functions - Schedule](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/schedule-functions)
- [Supabase Vault](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/vault)
- [Resend + Supabase](https://resend.com/docs/send-with-supabase-edge-functions)
- [Twilio Node.js](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/quickstart/node)

## Known Limitations

- **Spotify Development Mode**: Limited to 5 authorized users. Manual artist following works for all users. Spotify integration should be behind a feature flag until Extended Quota is approved.
- **No dedicated artists column on events table**: Matching runs against title + description. Adding a derived column is deferred to avoid modifying 141 scrapers.
- **Event descriptions may contain negations**: pg_trgm cannot detect negation. Accepted as a low-frequency edge case.

Build the notification preferences UI where users can configure which channels they want for artist alerts (in-app, email, SMS), provide a phone number for SMS, and see their current settings.

# fn-10-spotify-artist-alerts-follow-artists.2 Database Schema: followed_artists, artist_event_notifications, notification_preferences

## Description
Create the three new database tables (`followed_artists`, `artist_event_notifications`, `notification_preferences`), enable `pg_trgm` extension, add GIN indexes for matching performance, and write RLS policies. Also add a security fix: RLS policy on `profiles` to deny client-side SELECT of `spotify_refresh_token`.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `supabase/migrations/20260407_artist_alerts_schema.sql`, `src/types/database.ts`

## Approach

- Follow existing migration pattern in `supabase/migrations/`
- Enable `pg_trgm` extension with `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm`
- Create GIN trigram index on `events.title` for `gin_trgm_ops`
- Add `artist_name_normalized` as a generated column (lowercase, no diacritics) on `followed_artists`
- RLS: users can only CRUD their own rows in all three tables
- RLS: deny SELECT on `profiles.spotify_refresh_token` for authenticated role (only service_role can read)
- Update `src/types/database.ts` with TypeScript interfaces for new tables
- Unique constraint on `followed_artists(user_id, artist_name_normalized)` to prevent duplicate follows
- Unique constraint on `artist_event_notifications(user_id, event_id, artist_name)` for dedup

## Key context

- `pg_trgm` word_similarity operator `<%` uses default threshold 0.6 -- tune later in task .6
- The `notifications` table check constraint already includes `spotify_match` type -- no change needed
- The existing `spotify_artist_matches` table is NOT dropped (migration path handled in task .3)
- Austrian/German names need unaccent() -- check if `unaccent` extension is available in Supabase
## Acceptance
- [ ] `followed_artists` table created with all columns per ER diagram in epic spec
- [ ] `artist_event_notifications` table created with unique constraint on (user_id, event_id, artist_name)
- [ ] `notification_preferences` table created with unique constraint on user_id
- [ ] `pg_trgm` extension enabled
- [ ] GIN index on `events.title` using `gin_trgm_ops` for fast fuzzy matching
- [ ] RLS policies: users can only access their own rows in all three tables
- [ ] RLS policy: `spotify_refresh_token` column on `profiles` not readable by authenticated users
- [ ] TypeScript types in `src/types/database.ts` updated for all new tables

# fn-10-spotify-artist-alerts-follow-artists.4 Spotify Search API Integration with Client Credentials Flow

## Description
Add Spotify artist search API using Client Credentials flow (app-level token, no user context needed). This allows both Spotify-connected and non-connected users to search for artists to follow.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `src/app/api/artists/search/route.ts`, `src/lib/spotify.ts`

## Approach

- Add Client Credentials flow to `src/lib/spotify.ts`: `getClientCredentialsToken()` -- uses SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID + SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET to get app-level access token
- Cache the client credentials token in memory (1 hour TTL, refresh on expiry)
- New API route `GET /api/artists/search?q=<query>&limit=10`
  - Calls Spotify `GET /v1/search?type=artist&market=AT&q=<query>`
  - Returns: `{ artists: [{ id, name, image_url, genres, popularity }] }`
- Rate limit: debounce client-side (300ms), server-side max 20 requests per minute per user
- Auth required for the API route (prevents abuse)
- Handle Spotify 429 responses with `Retry-After` header

## Key context

- Client Credentials flow is different from Authorization Code flow -- it does NOT require user OAuth, only the app client_id + client_secret
- This works even in Spotify Development Mode (no user limit for app-level search)
- The `market=AT` parameter localizes results to Austria
- Existing `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID` and `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` env vars should already be set
## Acceptance
- [ ] `getClientCredentialsToken()` added to `src/lib/spotify.ts` with caching
- [ ] `GET /api/artists/search?q=<query>` returns Spotify artist search results
- [ ] Search works for all authenticated users (not just Spotify-connected)
- [ ] Results include artist id, name, image_url, genres, popularity
- [ ] Rate limiting: Spotify 429 responses handled gracefully with retry
- [ ] Auth required -- returns 401 for unauthenticated requests

data.title: Artist-Event Matching Engine with pg_trgm Word Similarity

tasks.spec:
# fn-10-spotify-artist-alerts-follow-artists.6 Artist-Event Matching Engine with pg_trgm Word Similarity

## Description
Build the artist-event matching engine using PostgreSQL pg_trgm word_similarity. This replaces the current naive `.includes()` matching with a robust, performant, fuzzy matching system that handles short names, diacritics, and substring matching.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `src/lib/artist-matching.ts`, `src/scripts/match-artists.ts`, tests

## Approach

- Create `src/lib/artist-matching.ts` with the core matching logic
- Matching strategy (tiered):
  1. Names < 3 chars: skip (too many false positives for "DJ", "M", etc.)
  2. Names 3 chars: exact word boundary match (case-insensitive, `~*` regex with `\m...\M`)
  3. Names 4+ chars: pg_trgm `word_similarity()` with threshold >= 0.6
- Normalization: lowercase, strip diacritics (reuse unaccent if available, else manual mapping for ae/oe/ue/ss)
- Query: match `followed_artists.artist_name_normalized` against `events.title` and `events.description`
- Only match future events (`start_date >= now()`)
- Deduplication: check `artist_event_notifications` unique constraint before insert
- Create CLI script `src/scripts/match-artists.ts` with `--dry-run` flag for testing
- Reuse Jaro-Winkler from `src/lib/dedup/jaro-winkler.ts` as secondary confirmation for borderline matches

## Key context

- The GIN index on `events.title` (created in task .2) is critical for pg_trgm performance
- `word_similarity()` checks if the query appears as a substring within the target -- perfect for "Bilderbuch" in "Bilderbuch Open Air Wien"
- Festival events may have 50+ artists in description -- each match generates a separate `artist_event_notifications` row but only ONE notification per (user, event)
- The `match_score` column stores the word_similarity score for later quality analysis
## Acceptance

# fn-10-spotify-artist-alerts-follow-artists.7 Post-Scrape Matching Pipeline: Edge Function and pg_cron

## Description
Build the automated matching pipeline that runs after scraping: a Supabase Edge Function triggered by pg_cron that matches all followed artists against newly inserted/updated events and creates notifications with fan-out to in-app, email, and SMS channels.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `supabase/functions/match-artists/index.ts`, `src/lib/notification-sender.ts`, migration for pg_cron job

## Approach

- Supabase Edge Function `match-artists`:
  - Queries `followed_artists` (all active follows across all users)
  - Queries events inserted/updated since last run (track via `last_run_at` in a config table or pg_cron metadata)
  - Runs matching engine (pg_trgm queries from task .6, executed as SQL from the Edge Function via supabase-js service_role)
  - Inserts new `artist_event_notifications` rows (skip existing via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)
  - For each new notification: insert into `notifications` table (type: `spotify_match`)
  - Fan-out: check `notification_preferences` per user, send email/SMS if enabled
- pg_cron schedule: every 2 hours (`0 */2 * * *`)
- Use `pg_net` to invoke the Edge Function from pg_cron
- Store Edge Function URL and service key in Supabase Vault
- Also create `src/lib/notification-sender.ts` as a shared module for sending notifications across channels (in-app is just an INSERT, email calls Resend, SMS calls Twilio)
- Add npm script `npm run match-artists` as fallback for manual execution

## Key context

- Edge Functions run Deno, not Node.js -- use Deno-compatible imports
- Edge Function timeout: 150s on free plan, should be enough for batch matching
- Use `EdgeRuntime.waitUntil()` for email/SMS sending (non-blocking background work)
- The `notifications` INSERT triggers Supabase Realtime automatically (NotificationBell picks it up)
- pg_cron requires `pg_cron` and `pg_net` extensions -- verify they are enabled
- Notification content: title = "Kuenstler-Alert: {artist_name}", body = "{artist_name} tritt bei {event_title} auf! {event_date} in {event_location}", action_url = "/events/{event_id}"

- [ ] pg_cron job scheduled to invoke the Edge Function every 2 hours

## Description
Integrate Resend for email notifications. Build email templates for artist alerts and wire into the notification sender module. Include GDPR-compliant unsubscribe mechanism.

## Approach

- Install `resend` npm package
- Create `src/lib/email.ts` with `sendArtistAlertEmail()` function
- Email template using React Email (or plain HTML): artist name, event title, date, location, link to event, unsubscribe link
- Unsubscribe link: `/api/notifications/unsubscribe?token=<jwt>` -- sets `channel_email=false` in `notification_preferences`
- Wire into `notification-sender.ts`: if user has `channel_email=true` and verified email, call Resend
- Env var: `RESEND_API_KEY`
- From address: `alerts@osterreich.events` (or whatever domain is configured)
- Error handling: retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff, log failures
- Rate limit: batch emails, max 100/day on Resend free tier

## Key context

- Resend has a Supabase Edge Function example -- but our notification-sender may run both in Edge Functions (Deno) and Node.js (npm script). Use `fetch()` directly instead of the npm package for Deno compatibility
- GDPR/DSGVO: email opt-in must be explicit (off by default in notification_preferences)
- User email comes from `auth.users.email` via Supabase Auth

# fn-10-spotify-artist-alerts-follow-artists.9 SMS Notification Service with Twilio Integration

## Description
Integrate Twilio for SMS notifications. Build SMS message formatting and wire into the notification sender module. Include opt-out handling and phone number validation.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `src/lib/sms.ts`, `src/lib/notification-sender.ts` (update)

## Approach

- Install `twilio` npm package (or use fetch for Deno compatibility)
- Create `src/lib/sms.ts` with `sendArtistAlertSMS()` function
- SMS format: "Kuenstler-Alert: {artist_name} tritt am {date} bei {event_title} in {location} auf! Details: {url}"
- Max 160 chars per SMS segment -- truncate event title if needed
- Phone number validation: E.164 format, Austrian numbers start with +43
- Wire into `notification-sender.ts`: if user has `channel_sms=true` and valid `phone_number`, call Twilio
- Env vars: `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER`
- Handle opt-out: if Twilio returns "STOP" keyword response, set `channel_sms=false`
- Error handling: retry up to 2 times, log undeliverable numbers

## Key context

- Twilio SMS costs money per message -- consider batching or rate limiting
- For Deno (Edge Function): use Twilio REST API via fetch, not the npm SDK
- Austrian mobile numbers: +43 6XX XXX XXXX
- SMS is the most intrusive channel -- only for users who explicitly opted in AND provided a phone number

- [ ] Phone number validated as E.164 format before sending
